summary: Initial discovery for StratusAI migrating high-volume chat and embedding workloads off OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Key concerns: latency parity, eval and output parity, model compatibility (vLLM/TGI stacks), infra/network/VPC connectivity, KMS and audit requirements. Action items include pricing, benchmark checklist, and scheduling a technical deep-dive with infra team.
topics: Latency and cost tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated)
Model compatibility and eval parity (OpenAI -> Redwood models)
vLLM/TGI runtime differences and infra implications
Security/compliance: SOC2, KMS, VPC/peering, data residency
Pilot and benchmark plan, success metrics
transcript:
00:00 Avery Clarke: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Avery from Redwood, AE on the account. Quick intros?
00:06 Maya Chen: Maya, CTO at StratusAI. We run a customer-facing chat agent and heavy embedding pipeline, lots of small requests, hey sorry my mic is a bit off.
00:13 Liam O'Connor: Liam, senior ML infra, I own model infra and cost optimization.
00:16 Priya Nair: Priya, security and compliance.
00:20 Avery Clarke: Awesome. Samir, want to do a quick overview of what Redwood Dedicated offers and then we'll dig into your migration concerns?
00:25 Samir Patel: Sure, super quick - Redwood Dedicated is reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, you get private networking options, KMS integrations, audit logs, and the same API surface as our hosted product. For migrations from OpenAI we usually try to cover compatibility, eval parity, and performance tuning - so, things like tokenization differences, prompt engineering noise, model variant parity, and runtime differences if you run v-LLM or TGI on-prem.
00:47 Maya Chen: Yeah, our big thing is output parity - we can't have customer-facing differences. We did a quick A/B and noticed some drift when switching models, not sure if that's quantization or prompt framing.
00:58 Samir Patel: Totally. We do model verification; usually we provide a parity eval harness. We'll run your eval set against the target model on Redwood Dedicated and measure stability metrics. There are sometimes subtle tokenizer and sampling param mismatches - and also if you go to quantized runtimes that can shift outputs a bit.
01:16 Liam O'Connor: We're currently using OpenAI gpt-4o so expectations on latency are tight - 95th p90 around 350ms for short chats. Cost is ballooning so exploring Dedicated for unit economics. Can Redwood hit similar p95s with dedicated infra?
01:28 Samir Patel: Yes, we commonly hit p95 in the 200-400ms range depending on seq length and batching. Key is kernel selection, batching policy, and KV cache strategy. For short chats we configure low-batch, low-queue windows to preserve latency. We'll need to see your request distribution to recommend shapes.
01:43 Diego Ramos: Quick infra Q - our network is locked down. Do you support VPC peering or a private endpoint? We also have a KMS that we need to integrate for customer-encrypted data.
01:52 Avery Clarke: Yes - Redwood Private/Dedicated supports VPC peering and private control plane options. KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys are part of the enterprise package; we can share network diagrams and an integration playbook.
02:05 Priya Nair: Also SOC2 and audit logs - we need logs for token-level access and redaction. How granular are the logs?
02:12 Samir Patel: Audit logs include request/response metadata and routing traces, retention configurable. We can redact PII; there are options for token-level metrics in observability. We'll share SOC2 documentation and certs.
02:25 Maya Chen: On the runtime side, we evaluated vLLM in-house and also tried TGI; we saw different memory characteristics. If Redwood runs its own runtime, will we be able to use our existing vLLM optimizations or is that incompatible?
02:38 Samir Patel: Redwood's serving runtime supports multiple execution paths; we support GGML-like kernels, vLLM-style KV cache optimizations and quantization profiles. For some community stacks like TGI there's subtle API and model format mangling, but usually we can ingest weights or provide conversion steps. We'll check model format for your checkpoints.
02:55 Liam O'Connor: Do you accept .safetensors from our pipeline? We do sharded checkpoints.
03:00 Samir Patel: Yes, safetensors are supported, sharded is fine; need to confirm shard layout but that's common. We'll have a model onboarding checklist.
03:08 Maya Chen: Eval parity - can you run our regression suite and give diffs and an acceptance threshold? We need something auditable to present to ops.
03:15 Samir Patel: Absolutely. Typical workflow: you hand us the eval set and evaluation scripts, we run on both hosted (or your baseline) and on a Dedicated pilot, produce side-by-side metrics (BLEU-ish, embedding cosine similarity, output deltas), and a human-sample review. We can surface examples where outputs differ and propose mitigation - prompt normalization, sampling params, or model variant adjustments.
03:38 Liam O'Connor: Another point - how do you handle model rollouts and fallbacks? We need canary and A/B for stable rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper hosted variant when Dedicated is saturated.
03:50 Samir Patel: We have routing policies - region, model variant, tier-based fallback. Canary rollouts and automatic fallback are supported; you can configure a fallback to hosted or lower-capacity nodes. We'll show the console routing UI in the demo.
04:04 Priya Nair: Encryption in flight and at rest? Do you manage keys when using Dedicated?
04:09 Avery Clarke: For Dedicated, keys can be customer-managed via KMS/HSM. In-flight is TLS; at-rest is disk encryption; if you need bring-your-own-keys that's supported for enterprise plans.
04:20 Maya Chen: Okay, for success criteria: parity within X% of our current scores on the eval suite, p95 latency <= 400ms for short seq, and cost reduction >= 30%. Is that reasonable?
04:33 Samir Patel: That sounds like a workable pilot success definition. We'll size the Dedicated pool and recommend quantization profiles - often INT8 for cost, FP16 for parity. We'll run benchmarks with your eval set to quantify the tradeoffs.
04:48 Diego Ramos: On the benchmark mechanics - do you need a VPC peering or can we just provide a sample dataset and run it through your hosted env first?
04:57 Samir Patel: Either works. For earliest results, run through hosted or a staging cluster; if you want exact networking behavior we'll set up a temporary VPC peering to a small Dedicated pilot. For throughput tests we'll want prereq permissions.
05:10 Maya Chen: Any gotchas with tokenization and system/bot messages? We send a lot of structured messages.
05:16 Samir Patel: Yep, system/narrative tokens can cause variance. We usually normalize prompts in the eval harness so it's apples-to-apples. Also beware of hidden sampling seeds or temperature differences - we replicate your sampling config.
05:30 Liam O'Connor: Pricing question - committed capacity vs burst? We need a predictable monthly bill but some spike capacity for product launches.
05:37 Avery Clarke: Dedicated supports reserved capacity with burst options. Contracts are monthly/annual; we'll include burst credits and overage policies in the pricing sheet. I'll send a few commitment tiers based on your current QPS and 99th percentile token rates.
05:52 Priya Nair: One compliance detail - do you provide SLA for data deletion and proof of deletion on contract end?
05:58 June Moreno: Yes, we have data lifecycle policies and can provide deletion certificates for contractual terms. We'll share the deletion workflow doc.
06:08 Maya Chen: Great. For timeline, we'd like a pilot in January if possible. Is that feasible?
06:13 Samir Patel: Yes, if we start onboarding in mid-December we can have a small pilot by mid-January. We'll need eval sets, model artifacts, and a PO for pilot access depending on contract terms.
06:22 Liam O'Connor: Who on your side will run the benchmark? Will Samir run it and produce a report or do you provide tooling for us to run locally against your endpoints?
06:29 Samir Patel: We can do both: provide a reproducible script you can run in your infra and also run on our side for a controlled comparison. We'll share the script and a small repro harness that runs the eval and outputs metrics and sample diffs.
06:42 Maya Chen: Good - please include human review steps in the report. Ops wants auditable examples.
06:47 Samir Patel: Will do.
06:49 Avery Clarke: Quick recap and next steps - I'll send pricing and capacity options, Samir will share benchmark checklist and repro script, and we'll schedule the technical deep-dive with Diego and Liam on Wed 2026-12-16. Priya to send compliance questionnaire. Anything else?
07:05 Priya Nair: We'll send a list of required certs and network constraints.
07:09 Diego Ramos: I'll coordinate VPC peering details if we go that route.
07:12 Maya Chen: Thanks, all. Looking forward to the pilot.
07:15 Avery Clarke: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up by EOD tomorrow with the initial docs.
07:20 [Call ends]

Notes on transcript: occasional transcription artifacts (v-LM/vLLM as v-LMM in a few spots), speaker overlap at times, proper nouns may be slightly off.
